## The question

At each visit $j = 0, \dots, K$ a clinician may prescribe a drug, $R(j) \in \{0, 1\}$,
and the patient may take it, $A(j) \in \{0, 1\}$. Taking it depends on things
we do not observe (motivation, frailty) that also affect the outcome $Y$, so
comparing those who took the drug with those who did not is confounded. The
prescription, on the other hand, is driven by what the clinician sees and
records: given the observed history $F_j = (\bar L(j), \bar A(j-1))$ it is as
good as random. It affects the outcome only through whether the drug is taken.

Intervening on the treatment directly is neither identified nor realistic.
What a health system can change is how often drugs are prescribed. The package
estimates
$$\psi(\alpha) = E\bigl[Y^{h^*_\alpha}\bigr], \qquad h^*_{\alpha,j}(1 \mid F_j) = \alpha\,\lambda_j(F_j),\quad \lambda_j(F_j) = P(R(j)=1 \mid F_j),$$
the mean outcome if prescriptions were $\alpha$ times as frequent as they are
now, for every type of patient.
- The intervention multiplies the intensity of the prescription process. It
  puts no mass where prescriptions never happen, so positivity holds for
  $\alpha \le 1$. For $\alpha > 1$ the probability is capped at 1 where
  $\alpha\lambda_j > 1$.
- Under the exclusion restriction, and if only the current prescription acts
  on the current treatment, $\psi(\alpha)$ is also the effect of the
  **implied** intervention on the treatment,
  $$g_j(\alpha)(F_j) = \pi_0(F_j) + \alpha\,\lambda_j(F_j)\,[\pi_1(F_j) - \pi_0(F_j)], \qquad \pi_r = P(A(j)=1 \mid R(j)=r, F_j).$$

  Only the part of treatment that responds to the prescription moves.

## A simulated example

`simulate_lii()` generates this structure with an unmeasured confounder `U`
of adherence and outcome, and censoring.

```{r}
library(impliedIV)
sim <- simulate_lii(n = 1500, K = 2, seed = 1)
head(sim$data)
d <- lii_data(sim$data, id = "id", time = "visit", instrument = "R", treatment = "A",
              outcome = "Y", covariates = "L", baseline = "W")
d
lii_describe(d)
```

The main analysis uses `learner = learner_hapc` (Highly Adaptive Principal
Components). Here `learner_glm` keeps the vignette fast.

```{r}
fit <- lii_tmle(d, alphas = c(0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.25, 1.5), learner = learner_glm, verbose = FALSE)
fit
```

```{r, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
plot(fit, diff = TRUE)
```

The true values of this simulation, by Monte Carlo:

```{r}
round(sim$truth(fit$estimates$alpha, n_mc = 2e5), 4)
```

## Diagnostics

```{r}
dg <- lii_diagnostics(fit)
dg$first_stage         # pi1 - pi0: strength of the instrument
dg$alpha_max_uncapped  # alphas above this are capped somewhere
dg$weights
```

## The implied intervention and an interpretable scale for alpha

```{r}
subset(fit$implied, visit == 0)
```

`implied_p_treat` averages $g_j(\alpha)$ over the observed histories. To
know how much more treatment each $\alpha$ means in the intervened world,
estimate the mean proportion of visits with treatment, and calibrate:

```{r}
ft <- lii_tmle(lii_treatment_outcome(d), alphas = fit$settings$alphas,
               learner = learner_glm, verbose = FALSE)
ft$estimates[, c("alpha", "estimate", "lower", "upper")]
calibrate_alpha(ft, ratio = c(1.1, 1.2))
```

## Inference

The standard errors of `lii_tmle()` come from the influence curve, treating
the estimated $\alpha\hat\lambda$ as the intervention: this is the
data-adaptive parameter. For the parameter defined with the true $\lambda$,
`lii_bootstrap()` refits everything in each resample.

## Checking "only the current instrument acts on the current treatment"

```{r}
lag_sufficiency_test(sim$data, "id", "visit", "R", "A", covariates = "L", lags = 1)$p_value
```

## Preference instruments

When the data contain prescriptions but no adherence, a common instrument is
the prescriber's preference. `preference_instrument()` computes it from an
order log:
- leaving the patient out;
- using only orders before the encounter;
- with a trend term.

Its lagged values can be tested with `lag_sufficiency_test()`. See
`AGENTS.md` for how this fits the estimator, which needs a binary instrument.
